variant: remote operation cockpit for Kobelco excavators
name: Kobelco K-DIVE remote operation system
summary: Remote operation system from Kobelco: an operator in a dedicated cockpit far from the site runs hydraulic excavators, with machine operating data used to improve the site. Offered as a service in Japan; Kobelco Europe is bringing it to Europe with Leica Geosystems and Xwatch and will test it at debris removal sites in Ukraine.

germany.statusNote: No offer for German or EU customers found. Kobelco Construction Machinery Europe B.V. announced a K-DIVE partnership with Leica Geosystems and Xwatch for Europe in March 2025 with live demonstrations planned at bauma 2025, and plans to install machines and K-DIVE cockpits in Ukraine from October 2026 under an MoU with UNDP. In Japan the system is offered as a service.

specs.label: Control
specs.value: excavators operated from a distant location via a dedicated cockpit
specs.quote: It enables excavators to be controlled from a distant location via a specialised cockpit.

specs.label: European version add-ons
specs.value: Leica 3D machine control with semi-automatic functions; Xwatch 3D avoidance zones that limit height, depth and slew
specs.quote: The system automatically controls height, depth, and slew movements, preventing collisions and ensuring safer remote operations.

specs.label: Offer in Japan
specs.value: remote operation and operating-data site improvement solution, currently offered as a service; switching between remote and autonomous operation not yet included
specs.quote: 重機の遠隔操作と自動運転の切替機能、自動運転の内容設定を遠隔操作で行える機能は、現在サービス提供中の「K-DIVE(R)」では提供していません。

notes: Remote operation system; the host machines are Kobelco hydraulic excavators (crawler tracks assumed; the sources do not state the undercarriage).
An autonomous loading mode was tested in 2023 but is not part of the service offered then.
The cockpit has an emergency stop used when people approach the machine in mixed areas (Ando Hazama test rules).

images.alt: Kobelco K-DIVE remote operation cockpit with seat and screens

evidence.task: From one cockpit, two excavators loaded soil into dump trucks, switching between remote operation and autonomous loading
evidence.where: Japan – Ando Hazama site in the MLIT field verification of automated and remote construction machinery
evidence.note: Autonomous mode was a development feature; travel and preparation were remote, repetitive loading was autonomous.

evidence.task: Remote-operated excavators for debris removal, with K-DIVE cockpits installed locally and local operators trained
evidence.note: Field testing planned from October 2026 under an MoU with UNDP; not yet confirmed as started.
